ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached circuit diagram shows an input A entering from the left into an upper switching path whose control terminal is labeled B. The node after this upper path continues to the right as the output Y. A lower switching path is connected between the output node and ground, and its control terminal is labeled B with an overbar, i.e. B̅. Reasoning by cases: When B=1, the upper B-controlled path from A to Y is on, and since B̅=0, the lower pull-down path to ground is off. Therefore Y follows A. When B=0, the upper path is off, and since B̅=1, the lower pull-down path is on, forcing Y=0. Thus Y equals A when B is 1 and equals 0 when B is 0, so Y = A·B.
